c74object.name: py_repl
c74object.description: An interactive Python console that runs code in the namespace of the py object named by py. Each submitted input runs at once and its output, results and tracebacks appear in the transcript above the input. The input has syntax highlighting, auto-indent, bracket matching, undo, history and completion from the names the namespace holds at runtime. History and the unsent input are saved with the patch.

inlet.description: Receives run, clear, history, themes and attribute messages.

method.name: (keyboard)
method.description:
Click the box to give it the focus, then:
Return: run the input when it is complete code and the caret is at its end; else a new line. A block (def, for, if, ...) ends with a blank line, as in the Python console.
Shift+Return: new line. Cmd+Return: run the input as it is.
Up/Down on the first or last input row: previous or next history entry. Down past the newest entry restores the unsent input. Elsewhere, Up/Down move by visual row.
Tab after a name or a dot: open the completion popup with the names the namespace holds now (math.fl lists floor), then names typed earlier in the console. In the popup: Up/Down select, Tab or Return accept, typing filters, Shift+Tab selects the previous item, Esc closes.
Tab elsewhere: indent. Shift+Tab: outdent.
Ctrl+C while code runs: stop it with KeyboardInterrupt. Ctrl+C otherwise: discard the input.
Cmd+K or Ctrl+L: clear the transcript. PageUp/PageDown: scroll.
Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z: undo, redo in the input. Cmd+X, Cmd+C, Cmd+V, Cmd+A: cut, copy, paste, select all.
With the transcript selected (after a click in it), Cmd+C copies and Cmd+A selects the transcript; any other key moves to the end of the input and types there.

method.name: (mouse)
method.description: Click and drag to select in the transcript or in the input; a drag stays in the part it started in. Double-click selects a word, triple-click a line. The wheel or trackpad scrolls (see scrollspeed). Right-click opens a menu: Copy, Paste, Select All, Clear Transcript and Clear History.

method.name: run
method.description: Runs the code as a submitted input: it is echoed in the transcript and added to the history. A single symbol is used as is; other arguments, such as run 1 + 2, are joined with spaces. Max splits a message at commas, so quote code that contains them: run "max(1, 2)".

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes the past input and output. The history is kept.

method.name: history
method.description: history clear forgets every entry, including those saved with the patch. history alone posts the number of entries.

method.name: themes
method.description: Posts the preset names and the one in use to the Max console.

attribute.name: py
attribute.digest: Name of the py object to run code in
attribute.description: The name of a py object. Default __main__, the first py created. It is looked up on every use, so the py object can be created, deleted or recreated at any time. The title strip shows not found when no py has the name, and abi mismatch when the py external is older than py_repl.

attribute.name: theme
attribute.description: Copies a preset over the color attributes and promptcolor: onedark (default), catppuccin, dracula, nord, gruvbox, monokai, solarized, the presets of py_code. Names ignore case, spaces, - and _. A color attribute saved with the box overrides the preset.

attribute.name: fontsize
attribute.description: Menlo, in points, clamped to 6-48. Default 12.

attribute.name: tabwidth
attribute.description: Spaces per indent level, for Tab, Shift+Tab and auto-indent, clamped to 1-16. Default 4.

attribute.name: autoclose
attribute.description: Typing an opening bracket or quote inserts its partner. Default 1.

attribute.name: completion
attribute.description: Tab after a name or a dot opens the completion popup. Off, Tab always indents. Default 1.

attribute.name: wrap
attribute.description: Wraps lines at the box width. Off, long lines are cut at the right edge. Default 1.

attribute.name: titlebar
attribute.description: The strip shows the history position while browsing and the py name with its link state. Default 1.

attribute.name: savehistory
attribute.digest: Save the history with the patch
attribute.description: Saves the last 200 entries, restored when the patch opens. Default 1.

attribute.name: maxlines
attribute.description: Lines kept in the transcript, clamped to 100-1000000; older lines are dropped in batches once it grows a quarter past the limit. Default 10000.

attribute.name: scrollspeed
attribute.description: Multiplies the scroll delta, clamped to 0.05-50. Default 3.

attribute.name: promptcolor
attribute.description: RGBA. Default and theme changes: the theme's comment color.

attribute.name: textcolor
attribute.digest: Text color (output, results and untagged code)

attribute.name: curlinecolor
attribute.description: Kept so themes and copied attributes match py_code.

attribute.name: builtincolor
attribute.digest: Builtin color (print, len, None, True, False)

attribute.name: escapecolor
attribute.digest: Escape sequence and f-string brace color

attribute.name: commentcolor
attribute.description: Comments in code, and notices such as KeyboardInterrupt after Ctrl+C or not found. RGBA. Default from theme.

attribute.name: matchcolor
attribute.digest: Matching bracket highlight in the input

attribute.name: blinkcolor
attribute.description: Kept so themes and copied attributes match py_code.

attribute.name: barhighlight
attribute.description: Kept so themes and copied attributes match py_code.

attribute.name: warningcolor
attribute.description: Kept so themes and copied attributes match py_code.

c74object.discussion: py_repl calls the linked py object directly, not through patch cords, and has no outlets. Code runs on Max's main thread, so py's api module can be used freely, but the patch UI (drawing, mouse, keys) waits until a run ends, and output appears then. Audio and, with Overdrive on, scheduled events keep running. Keys typed during a run are kept. Ctrl+C stops a run between Python bytecodes: time.sleep and long calls into C code, such as numpy or file reads, finish first. It acts only while Max is the frontmost app. The interrupt reaches whatever Python code the main thread runs, so if the code triggered another py object through its outlet, that object's call is the one stopped. The py object's security_mode applies to code run here.
